behaviors.protocol_context: Leader term and current voter configuration
behaviors.trigger: Accepted MsgAppResp or switchToConfig calls maybeCommit
reads: Peer Match indexes, voter sets, current term, local log term at quorum index
important_branches: maybeCommit advances only beyond previous committed index at a nonzero matching current term.
MsgAppResp success that updates progress and advances commitment invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages and bcastAppend.
switchToConfig advancing commitment calls bcastAppend without invoking releasePendingReadIndexMessages.
unknowns: Whether another guaranteed trigger releases previously queued reads when switchToConfig supplies the first current-term commit.

behaviors.execution_owner: raft Step, campaign, role transition methods
behaviors.trigger: Election campaign, higher-term message, or role transition
reads: Message term and type, lease interval, local vote, last log identity
writes: Term, Vote, role, leader, progress, readOnly state
important_branches: reset preserves Vote within a term and clears it on term change; resets progress and readOnly but not the committed log prefix.
Pre-candidate transition does not increment term or reset Vote.
Lower-term ordinary responses return before role-specific consumption. Lower-term storage append responses do not stabilize entries but may acknowledge a snapshot.
Actual votes require canVote and an up-to-date candidate log; response publication uses msgsAfterAppend.

behaviors.protocol_context: Ready batch, synchronous or asynchronous storage mode
writes: Ready messages and storage work; stepsOnAdvance; accepted unstable/application work
async_boundaries: Host persists entries, HardState and snapshots; external storage completion is not established by Ready emission.
Async mode issues local storage messages; synchronous mode places self-responses into stepsOnAdvance and publishes non-self deferred responses in Ready.Messages.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Append acknowledgments are queued behind persistence by send; leader self-ack is also deferred.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Vote responses are queued behind persistence before becoming usable election support.

unknowns: Exact async response construction and application scheduling still need tracing.

facts.meaning: The leader commit boundary has advanced to a log index whose term matches its current term, based on current voter Match aggregation. This alone does not establish that pending reads were released or entries were applied.
facts.validity_context: Leader-side maybeCommit with current tracker configuration. The committed prefix survives role changes, while the assertion that its term equals the current term must be reevaluated after a term change.
facts.durability: In-memory commit advancement; host persistence and application completion are separate.
facts.recovery: Restart reconstruction is not yet traced.
unknowns: ReadIndex consumption and application consumption of committed history remain to be mapped.

surfaces.reason: Unlike MsgAppResp commitment advancement, configuration-driven advancement does not directly release pending ReadIndex messages. Determine a legal history and alternative release triggers before attributing a wakeup duty.

doc.go permits sending messages while entries in the same batch persist, while rawnode.go states Ready requires persistence before sending. Determine actual Ready/Node contracts and whether response publication needs stricter host ordering.

formation.explanation: Leader proposals receive term/index, append to the log and queue a persistence-delayed self acknowledgment. Peer acknowledgments update progress; tracker aggregates current voters using both majorities for joint configuration, then maybeCommit checks the current log term before advancing commitment. Acknowledgment-driven advancement broadcasts append and releases queued reads, while configuration-driven advancement broadcasts without that release.

context.explanation: Campaign transitions establish candidate term and self vote; vote eligibility uses local vote/leader context and log freshness. PreVote leaves term and vote unchanged. Step handles message terms before role handlers, with explicit pre-vote/lease exceptions and lower-term rejection. Role reset clears accumulated progress and readOnly context while preserving the committed prefix.

connection.explanation: Term dispatch prevents ordinary old responses from becoming new leader support. Persistence-delayed vote/append replies and leader self replies connect durable support to election and commit decisions. Configuration application reinterprets peer progress through a changed voter set and may itself advance commitment; established committed history constrains snapshots and subsequent log repair.

open_details: Pending-read release following configuration-driven first current-term commit.
